sections.label: Debate on both Bills
sections.summary: Members may raise questions or views on both Bills during the debate, with a formal Second Reading of the IRDA Bill to meet procedural requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Members will be welcome to raise questions or express their views on both Bills during the debate.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will still have the formal Second Reading of the IRDA Bill to ensure that procedural requirements are met.

sections.label: COVID-19 support measures committed
sections.summary: About S$100 billion, roughly 20% of GDP, was committed to COVID-19 support measures, which DPM Heng said averted a 5.6% real GDP loss and saved an average of 155,000 jobs yearly in 2020 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Around S$100 billion has been committed in support measures to deal with COVID-19 or assist people in the face of the impact of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This amounts to about 20% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Just last month, in Parliament, Deputy Prime Minister Heng observed that the relief measures have helped avert a 5.6% loss in real GDP this year and they would have helped save an average of 155,000 jobs each year, in 2020 and 2021.

sections.label: Moratorium extension periods
sections.summary: Except for construction and supply contracts, options and sale and purchase agreements with developers, and event and tourism-related contracts, the moratorium for other contracts is extended one month, expiring 19 November.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Save for construction and supply contracts, options and sale and purchase agreements with developers and event and tourism-related contracts, which will be extended for longer periods, the moratorium for the other types of contracts are extended only for a month and will expire on 19 November.

sections.label: Impact on tourism sector businesses
sections.summary: This would continue to significantly impact some businesses, affecting over 20,000 businesses in the tourism, hospitality, conventions and exhibitions sectors alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This would continue to significantly impact some businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This affects roughly over 20,000 businesses in the tourism, hospitality, conventions, exhibitions sectors – in those sectors alone, 20,000.

sections.label: Nightlife establishments and workers
sections.summary: Many of the 1,300 nightlife establishments employ around 20,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Take for example many of the 1,300 nightlife establishments, which employ around 20,000 workers.

sections.label: Nightlife shutdown risk and assistance
sections.summary: A Singapore Nightlife Business Association poll found over 90% of respondents saw at least a 50% chance of wholly shutting down if they did not reopen soon, and MTI will provide an assistance package for nightlife businesses to transit out and pivot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: According to a poll by the Singapore Nightlife Business Association, over 90% of respondents said there was at least a 50% chance of them wholly shutting down, if they did not reopen soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For nightlife businesses, MTI will be providing an assistance package for them to transit out and pivot to new areas should they choose, and will be announcing more details soon.

sections.label: SME revenue falls and insolvencies
sections.summary: SMEs with significant revenue falls are about five times the 2019 number, and insolvency proceedings are expected to rise correspondingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The number of SMEs who have experienced a significant revenue fall on a rough estimate is about five times what it was in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And we can expect the number of insolvency proceedings to substantially increase correspondingly.

sections.label: Simplified Insolvency Programme for small businesses
sections.summary: The IRDA Bill introduces a Simplified Insolvency Programme to help small businesses restructure debts, liquidate and distribute assets efficiently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, the IRDA Bill will put in place amendments to introduce a Simplified Insolvency Programme, SIP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This will make it easier for small businesses to restructure their debts, liquidate, and also distribute their assets in an orderly, effective and efficient manner.

sections.label: Re-Align Framework for COVID-19-hit businesses
sections.summary: The Re-Align Framework helps small businesses badly hit by COVID-19 restrictions renegotiate, or terminate contracts on a no-fault basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Re-Align Framework seeks to help small businesses substantially impacted by COVID-19 restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These are businesses that have been faring badly, little leverage and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It provides a framework to renegotiate, failing which the contract may be terminated on a no-fault basis in a manner that gives a fair and just outcome.

sections.label: Right to renegotiate and terminate contracts
sections.summary: Affected businesses may demand renegotiation, and if no agreement is reached, terminate contracts on a no-fault basis without substantial damages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Framework therefore seeks to solve this issue by giving the affected business the right to demand renegotiation from the counterparty, as a start.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And second, unless agreement is reached, an eligible business will have the right to terminate the contract on a no-fault basis without having to pay substantial damages in penalties for compensation in the manner that I had outlined earlier – for example, in relation to the unexpired balance period of the tenancy.

sections.label: First criterion is revenue
sections.summary: The first limb of Part 3 of the Second Schedule states the first criterion will be by revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The first limb of Part 3 of the Second Schedule of the Bill states that the first criteria will be by revenue.

sections.label: Eligibility by revenue fall
sections.summary: The second limb of Part 3 of the Second Schedule determines eligibility by the fall in revenue over a prescribed period compared to a pre-pandemic period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Indeed, Sir, it should not be difficult to identify a business that has been badly affected by COVID-19 and that is what we have done – to set an objective financial threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, in the second limb of Part 3 of the Second Schedule of the Bill, eligibility will be determined by the fall in revenue it has suffered over a prescribed period compared to a relevant comparable period prior to the pandemic.

sections.label: Singapore law and timing conditions
sections.summary: A contract must be governed by Singapore law, have a party with a Singapore place of business, and be entered into before 25 March 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, it must be governed by Singapore law and at least one of the parties must have a place of business in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, it must have been entered into before 25 March 2020.

sections.label: Three categories of specified contracts
sections.summary: Specified Contracts cover non-residential property leases or licences up to five years, goods or services supply contracts, and commercial equipment hire purchase and conditional sale agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The first type of specific contract are leases or licences for non-residential property in Singapore that have terms not exceeding five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The second relates to contracts for the supply of goods or services and these contracts are often at the centre of a business' operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The third category of Specified Contracts comprises hire purchase and conditional sale agreements for commercial equipment, including commercial vehicles.

sections.label: Commercial equipment rental agreements
sections.summary: The fourth category of Specified Contracts comprises rental agreements for commercial equipment, including commercial vehicles such as taxis and private hire cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The fourth category comprises rental agreements for commercial equipment, including commercial vehicles such as taxis and private hire cars.

sections.label: Notice of Negotiation and negotiation period
sections.summary: Party A must serve a Notice of Negotiation on Party B within six weeks, followed by a mandatory four-week negotiation period during which no assessor application can be made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Parties really ought not drag it out and there should not be uncertainty for a prolonged period as to whether a counterparty might end up wanting to terminate the contract or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Thus, to invoke this relief, the business which is defined as Party A in the Bill must serve a Notice of Negotiation on Party B, the counterparty, within a six-week window.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, after the Notice of Negotiation is served, there will be a mandatory four-week period for the parties to negotiate, during which no application can be made to the assessor.

sections.label: Assessor's determination on disagreement
sections.summary: Either party may apply to an Assessor if they disagree on the Framework's application, and the Assessor's determination is final, binding and non-appealable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Fourth, either Party can apply for an Assessor's determination if there is any disagreement on the application of the Framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, if after you have terminated or you are trying to work out the terms and you are unable to settle on the consequences of termination, for instance, then the parties may apply to an Assessor and the Assessor's determination in those cases will be final, binding and non-appealable.

sections.label: SRS instalment payment for arrears
sections.summary: The SRS lets these businesses pay outstanding arrears from a specified period in equal monthly instalments for up to 18 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They cannot just, say, give up the vehicle and go back to where it was because that is the tools of their trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These businesses will benefit from the SRS which will allow them to pay outstanding arrears from a specified period in equal instalments every month for up to 18 months.

sections.label: State intervention in contracts
sections.summary: A state may intervene in contracts to safeguard vital interests where a significant part of the economy is at stake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, a state may intervene in contracts, to fulfill its duty to safeguard vital interests of its people, where a significant part of the economy is at stake, and strict enforcement of a particular contractual rights could lead to damage to the whole economy.

sections.label: Extraordinary measure, once in a lifetime
sections.summary: The Government did not often intervene to this extent, calling it an extraordinary measure for a once in a lifetime event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Often in those cases, we did not intervene to this extent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I therefore emphasise again that this is an extraordinary measure that the Government has taken carefully as a reaction to a once in a lifetime event of unprecedented proportions.

sections.label: Consequences calibrated, debts remain payable
sections.summary: Consequences will be calibrated and modelled on established legal principles, and outstanding debts will remain payable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The nature of the consequences, even if one qualifies, will be calibrated and modelled on established legal principles as I have outlined, and outstanding debts will remain payable.

sections.label: Assessor considers tenant doing well
sections.summary: If a tenant is doing well, the Assessor can take that into account and make directions including additional compensation on termination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If the facts show, for example, that a tenant is, in reality doing well, the Assessor can take that into account, make the appropriate directions, including additional compensation that can be paid on termination.

sections.label: COVID-19 insolvencies and small enterprises
sections.summary: Researchers forecast global business insolvencies to rise 35% in 2021, and Singapore had over 250,000 micro and small enterprises in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, researchers have forecasted global business insolvencies to increase by 35% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In Singapore, in 2018, there were over 250,000 micro and small enterprises.

sections.label: Share of Singapore enterprise framework
sections.summary: Together they form about 95% of Singapore's enterprise framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Together they form about 95% of Singapore's enterprise framework.

sections.label: Simplified Insolvency Programme for small companies
sections.summary: The Bill introduces a Simplified Insolvency Programme with two temporary processes, including restructuring debts of viable micro and small companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Applying tailored processes to these micro and small companies however could help these companies get back on their feet in the same way as Swee Hong, which has benefited from IRDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This Bill, Sir, therefore, introduces a Simplified Insolvency Programme comprising two bespoke temporary processes to better suit the needs of micro and small companies: First, to restructure the debts of viable companies to rehabilitate their businesses.

sections.label: Intended six-month first instance period
sections.summary: Subject to further consultation and review, the intended period is six months at first instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Subject to further consultation and review, we intend for this at first instance to be six months.

sections.label: Eligibility requirements for simplified process
sections.summary: Requirements include liabilities not exceeding $2 million, 30 employees, 50 creditors, realisable amount not exceeding $50,000, and no other insolvency process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The requirements are intended to ensure that only cases that are suitable for this simplified process are accepted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: These requirements include a limit on the total liabilities of the company, not exceeding $2 million; limits on the number of creditors and employees, not exceeding 30 employees and 50 creditors respectively; the amount realisable in the winding up, not exceeding $50,000 and the company is not in the midst of any other debt restructuring or, otherwise, some other form of insolvency process.

sections.label: Court approval of compromise or arrangement
sections.summary: The company may apply under new section 72M(1), and the Court may approve only with agreement of two-thirds in value of creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The company may make an application under the new section 72M(1) for approval of the proposed compromise or arrangement an,d the Court may only approve the compromise or arrangement if there is an agreement of a majority of two-thirds in value of creditors.

sections.label: Related party votes and creditor classes
sections.summary: The Court must disregard related parties' agreement, and there will be three classes: secured, preferential unsecured, and unsecured ordinary creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In looking at whether the threshold is met, the Court must disregard the agreement or disagreement of any related party of the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, you cannot have a company which has several creditors who are related to officers of the company come together and decide on an outcome and use that consensus or agreement to bind the other creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There will be three classes in the scheme: secured creditors, preferential unsecured creditors and unsecured ordinary creditors.

sections.label: Programme shelf life of 90 days
sections.summary: Section 72Q provides that the programme will have a shelf life of 90 days at first instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Section 72Q provides that the programme will have a shelf life in the first instance of 90 days.

sections.label: Simplified winding up programme
sections.summary: Part 10A of the IRDA Bill establishes a simplified winding up programme that a company may resolve to be wound up voluntarily under.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Part 10A of the IRDA Bill establishes a simplified winding up programme, which a company may resolve to be wound up voluntarily under.

sections.label: Official Receiver as liquidator
sections.summary: The Official Receiver is the liquidator of the company under the new section 250K(3).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Official Receiver is the liquidator of the company under the new section 250K(3).

sections.label: Minister exempting licensed insolvency practitioners
sections.summary: A miscellaneous amendment under section 50 of IRDA empowers the Minister to exempt individuals from being qualified persons to be licensed insolvency practitioners, exercised judiciously case-by-case in exceptional justified cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is a miscellaneous amendment introduced under the existing section 50 of IRDA and it seeks to empower the Minister to exempt any individual from the requirement of being a qualified person in order to be a licensed insolvency practitioner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This power will be exercised judiciously, on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is not intended to allow a person to circumvent the general requirements but it is intended to be used in exceptional cases, where the exemption is justified.

sections.label: Re-Align and simplified insolvency frameworks
sections.summary: The Re-Align Framework lets businesses renegotiate and re-base contracts, while the simplified insolvency framework gives eligible companies an easier route to restructure, rehabilitate or exit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At the level of individual contracts – business to business, party to party – the Re-Align Framework will allow businesses to have a basis to renegotiate and re-base their contracts to adapt to substantially changed circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At the corporate level, the simplified insolvency framework will allow eligible companies an easier route to restructure or rehabilitate, or to exit in the way I have just outlined.

sections.label: Support for firms during COVID-19
sections.summary: Beyond Jobs Support Scheme salaries and foreign worker levy waivers and rebates, a $1.36 billion construction support package was extended, and the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act gives temporary relief against stipulated legal action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Beyond supporting salaries of local employees through the Jobs Support Scheme and providing significant foreign worker levy waivers and rebates, we have extended a $1.36 billion construction support package to construction firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Through the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act, firms also have temporary relief against stipulated legal action.

sections.label: Developer and purchaser relief measures
sections.summary: Developers received extension on project completion period and additional buyer's stamp duty remission timelines, while developers were prohibited from withholding or forfeiting booking fees during the relief period unless an assessor determines otherwise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For developers, we provided an extension on the project completion period and additional buyer's stamp duty remission timelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To protect purchasers, we prohibited developers from withholding or forfeiting any part of the booking fee paid by purchasers under the option to purchase during the relief period unless determined otherwise by an assessor.

sections.label: Universal EOT for construction contracts
sections.summary: Part 8A of the Bill provides a universal extension of time of four months for construction contracts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, Part 8A of the Bill will provide a universal extension of time, or EOT, of four months for construction contracts.

sections.label: Rental relief claim amount and cap
sections.summary: The amount is 50% of total qualifying cost or 0.2% of the contract sum, whichever is lesser, capped at 1.8% of the contract sum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The amount will either be 50% of the total qualifying cost for anything done for or provided to or enjoyed by the clients in the specified period or 0.2% of the contract sum whichever is lesser.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But the total amount that may be claimed under this mechanism is capped at 1.8% of the contract sum.

sections.label: Developer delivery date extension notice
sections.summary: Under Part 8C, developers facing COVID-19 construction delay may serve notice for an extension of the delivery date by up to four months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Under Part 8C, developers who have faced construction delay due to COVID-19 and require relief may serve a notice for an extension of the delivery date by up to four months, in line with the EOT for construction projects that I described earlier.

sections.label: Property Tax Rebate for non-residential properties
sections.summary: The Government introduced a Property Tax Rebate for Year 2020 for non-residential properties in the Unity Budget on 18 February 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Members will recall that to help businesses affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, the Government introduced a Property Tax Rebate for Year 2020 for non-residential properties, in the Unity Budget on 18 February 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Depending on the category of non-residential property, owners are granted a Property Tax Rebate of 30% to 100%.

sections.label: Rental waiver for SME and NPO tenants
sections.summary: For SME or specified NPO tenant-occupiers, the rental relief framework effects rental waiver from April to at most July 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Specifically, if the tenant-occupier is an SME or a specified Non-Profit Organisation or NPO, the rental relief framework effects rental waiver for the period from April to at most July 2020, depending on the type of property.

sections.label: Regulations to account for rent waived
sections.summary: The Bill enables the Minister for Finance to make regulations so the obligation to pass on the Property Tax Rebate takes into account rent waived under the rental relief framework.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The issue that arises is that the existing PT Rebate Regulations do not take into account the rental relief framework, and this could result in unintended consequences, such as when there is a change of tenants during the year and the property owner is subject to the rental relief framework.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, this Bill and the provisions in this Bill enables the Minister for Finance to make new or revised regulations, so as to ensure that the obligation to pass on the benefit of the Property Tax Rebate will take into account the rent waived under the rental relief framework.

sections.label: Insolvency amendments and moratorium
sections.summary: The amendments create a cheaper insolvency process allowing a company with special resolution and creditor support to get a moratorium and repay creditors while operating.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, these latest amendments provide a more efficient and cheaper insolvency process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These amendments permit a company with the support of a special resolution – 75% of shareholders and two-thirds of its creditors in support – to apply to the Official Receiver to come under this regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Once these parties agree, it can go into this process and get a moratorium on its liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Additionally, if the business is viable, it would be able to enter into a process similar to a scheme of arrangement which allows the management to stay in place and operate the company with a view to repaying creditors through operating the company.

sections.label: Section 42 termination mechanism
sections.summary: A new COVID-19 amendment provides a mechanism under section 42 letting businesses terminate obligations they otherwise could not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One of the features in the new latest COVID-19 amendments is a mechanism under section 42, which actually allows businesses to terminate obligations they would not otherwise be able to.

sections.label: Option to terminate leases
sections.summary: The amendment gives companies an option to terminate leases they otherwise lack, which the Bill hopes will let them renegotiate existing obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, what this amendment does is that it actually gives companies like that an option to terminate the lease if they want to, an option they do not otherwise have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But what the Bill also hopes to for is that giving companies this option to terminate will allow them to renegotiate their existing obligations.

sections.label: Landlord burden and negotiation timelines
sections.summary: The passage asks how landlords are protected from unfair burden, notes six weeks to invoke and four weeks to negotiate, and asks about vacant properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How will the framework ensure that landlords are not unfairly burdened by the termination of leases?

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Second, businesses will have six weeks to decide whether to invoke the framework and parties will have four weeks to negotiate, failing which the contract may terminate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Is it envisioned that landlords will face a sudden increase in vacant properties within a short timeframe?

sections.label: Restoring bankruptcy and insolvency measures
sections.summary: With COVID-19 Temporary Relief expiring 19 November and the Moratorium ended 19 October, the speaker proposes restoring Part 2 measures for worst hit sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: With the “COVID-19 Temporary Relief” set to expire on 19 November, a large number of lawsuits are being prepared as a consequence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Similarly, the Moratorium which ended on 19 October will likely lead to a large number of bankruptcies and insolvencies through legal actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One, for some of the worst hit sectors, I propose restoring Part 2 of the Temporary Relief Bill, namely, the prescribed measures relating to bankruptcy and insolvency, for at least several more months.

sections.label: Bankruptcy consequences for directors
sections.summary: The passage lists personal bankruptcy consequences including a three-year directorship ban, $500 borrowing limit, travel restrictions and three-year credit records.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Personal consequences include: (a) not being able to serve as a director of another company for a period of three years; (b) not being able to borrow more than $500; (c) not being able to travel without permission; (d) credit bureaus also to keep the bankruptcy records for three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Given that COVID-19 was something that was thrust upon these sectors, I hope our Government can, at least on a temporary basis, reduce the consequences for the directors of these badly affected sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Speaker, we can and must do more to give more time for our badly affected sectors to work out the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: In business, insolvency is always a distinct possibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: But in these worst hit sectors, what we are seeing for SMEs is a mass extinct event, an unpredictable collective disaster not easily foreseeable.

sections.label: Support for both Bills
sections.summary: The speaker gives full support for both Bills despite earlier points.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding my points, I give my full support for both Bills.

sections.label: Construction contract delivery stay
sections.summary: Construction contracts are afforded a stay of up to 122 days for delivery.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Construction contracts, in particular, are afforded a stay of up to 122 days for delivery.

sections.label: Moratorium 55-day floor proposal
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the moratorium should afford a default 55-day floor, consistent with the circuit breaker period.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since the circuit breaker period coincided with a forced cessation of a wide range of economic activity, it strikes me that the moratorium should afford a default of a 55-day floor, which is consistent with the circuit breaker period.

sections.label: Flexibility on threshold values
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes added flexibility since it is difficult to ascertain whether values like the $10 million sales turnover threshold are optimal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Since it is difficult to ascertain whether these values, such as the threshold for sales turnover is set at $10 million, are optimal, the added flexibility is most welcomed.

sections.label: 30-employee threshold comparison
sections.summary: The Bill's 30-employee threshold would encompass medium sized businesses in Australia but only small firms in the EU and US.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The 30-employee threshold specified in the Bill, for instance, would encompass medium sized businesses in Australia but constitute only small firms in the EU and US.

sections.label: Tiered bankruptcy rules consideration
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering tiered bankruptcy rules for micro, small, medium and large enterprises given difficulty defining enterprise types.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Rather, given the inherent difficulty of establishing what constitutes a micro and small enterprise, and by extension, the nature of the firms which may be able to endure more complex restructuring and dissolution procedures, it may be valuable to consider the possibility of a tiered set of bankruptcy rules that apply to micro, small, medium and large enterprises, consistent with the likely complexity of the operations.

sections.label: Zombie firms and bankruptcy procedures
sections.summary: Excessively forgiving bankruptcy procedures can delay foreclosures, letting zombie firms keep operating, which Minister Edwin Tong said harms economic vibrancy and other firms' growth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Excessively forgiving bankruptcy procedures can delay foreclosures on non-performing loans, enabling firms that would otherwise fail to keep operating.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Such zombie firms, as Minister Edwin Tong clarified, can be detrimental to economic vibrancy and can inhibit the growth of other non-zombie firms, as the experience of Japan in the 1990s amply demonstrates.

sections.label: Support for both Bills
sections.summary: The speaker supports both Bills despite the additional points of feedback.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding these additional points of feedback, I do support both Bills.

sections.label: Simplified Insolvency Programme purpose
sections.summary: The Simplified Insolvency Programme seeks to help businesses recover quickly, restructure debt to keep going, or have a simplified orderly exit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, the Simplified Insolvency Programme or SIP seeks to help businesses that need to recover quickly, restructure their debt obligations to keep the businesses going or to have a simplified and orderly exit if there is no better alternative.

sections.label: Revenue drop criteria calibration
sections.summary: For the amendment Bill to be helpful, the revenue drop criteria should not be too conservative, else only deeply indebted companies facing imminent solvency issues are covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Further, for this amendment Bill to be helpful, the criteria for the revenue drop should not be too conservative, else it would only cover companies that are already deeply in the red, facing imminent solvency issues.

sections.label: Clarification on entity eligibility
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify whether such entities can still benefit from this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can Minister clarify whether such entities can still benefit from this Bill?

sections.label: Calibrating criteria for policy intent
sections.summary: For the Bills' policy intent to work on the ground, criteria need appropriate calibration, a conservative but not overly conservative starting point, and sufficient latitude for expert assessors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For the policy intent of these Bills to be effective on the ground, the various criteria need to be calibrated appropriately where a conservative starting point ought to be held without being too conservative should be considered and sufficient latitude be given to the expert assessors to achieve a just and fair outcome for deserving cases.

sections.label: IRDA Bill lowers creditor threshold
sections.summary: The IRDA Bill lowers the creditor approval threshold for a Scheme of Arrangement from 75% to two-thirds in value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the IRDA Bill lowers the threshold vote from creditors required to commence restructuring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Currently, approval from a majority of creditors holding 75% in value of the debt owed must be obtained to approve a Scheme of Arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This Bill lowers the threshold from 75% to two-thirds.

sections.label: Fast-track process six-month limit
sections.summary: The Bill's fast-track process is limited to six months, though COVID-19 effects on small- and medium-sized MNCs may exceed this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fourth, although the fast-track process introduced by the Bill is limited to just six months, it is very possible that the effects of COVID-19 on small- and medium-sized MNCs will exceed this duration.

sections.label: Four-month universal extension of time
sections.summary: A universal extension of time of four months addresses this uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The universal extension of time of four months addresses this uncertainty.

sections.label: Programme for small companies restructuring
sections.summary: The programme assists small companies with simpler, faster, lower cost proceedings, such as simplified debt restructuring requiring one Court application instead of two.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: The programme focuses on assisting small companies by providing simpler, faster and lower cost proceedings for eligible companies, for example, for simplified debt restructuring, requiring one Court application, instead of two Court applications in a typical scheme of arrangement.

sections.label: Programme intent and worker position
sections.summary: The programme may help businesses rehabilitate and preserve jobs, but does not significantly improve the position of workers owed salaries or retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: For simplified debt restructuring, it may help certain businesses rehabilitate and survive this economic downturn which, in turn may help to preserve certain jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: However, as the primary intent of the programme is to assist troubled companies, it, therefore, means that the programme does not significantly improve the position of workers with owed salaries or retrenchment benefits.

sections.label: 175 workers' uncertain fate
sections.summary: The fate of 175 workers remains uncertain as they are unsecured and rank low in debt priority if liquidation goes ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: First, for the 175 workers, a number long-serving and loyal, their fate remains uncertain, as they are unsecured and, as such, rank low in the priority of debts if the liquidation goes ahead.

sections.label: SME contract renegotiation concerns
sections.summary: Members raise SME hardship from contract terms, urge renegotiation parameters, caution on contractual sanctity, and ask about recourse from assessor decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Forcing them to continue with those terms or face liquidated damages would cause severe hardship to many SMEs and micro-SMEs, especially those who just started business before COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: As such, this ability to renegotiate will go some way to help many of these SMEs and micro-SMEs stay in business and re-balance themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In this regard, can MinLaw consider outlining certain set parameters for renegotiation which can help as many of these companies as possible?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding – although this renegotiation sounds plausible – I submit that we need to tread carefully and with caution and limit the scope of what we can and are able to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This is to ensure that the fundamental principle of contractual sanctity is upheld and not undermined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I have residents as well as fellow practitioners who have given me feedback and raised questions and eyebrows over some of the decisions made by the assessors where a claim or dispute is brought before them under this Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am aware the decision of the assessors is final but is there any other recourse which can be taken in the event where a decision is manifestly prejudicial against a non-offending or innocent party?

sections.label: Re-Align Framework contract renegotiation
sections.summary: The Re-Align Framework lets affected businesses renegotiate and rebase contracts, failing which contracts may be terminated with prospective obligations extinguished.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Now that this context has changed, we need to provide a fair and transparent way to redesign these contracts that leads to a win-win situation for all contracting parties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This provision of the Re-Align Framework in COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment No 3) ensures that these contracts entered earlier do not allow one party to subject the other to a disproportionate financial and legal distress arising from COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In other words, the framework allows affected businesses to renegotiate and rebase their contracts, failing which the contracts may be terminated with prospective obligations extinguished.

sections.label: Rental relief and simplified insolvency
sections.summary: A member proposes extending rental relief categories to other debts and notes the simplified insolvency programme allows eligible companies to restructure debts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Earlier in my maiden speech, I also spoke on how the rental relief framework for SMEs have been beneficial, providing peace of mind for our businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I propose an extension of the categories within the current rental relief framework to include other debts so that it provides businesses with a longer runway to pay their debts while attempting to restart their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The simplified insolvency programme in the IRDA Bill provides this process for the restructuring of debts to any eligible company that seeks to enter into a compromise or an arrangement between the company and its creditors or any class of those creditors.

sections.label: SIP and Re-Align Framework assistance
sections.summary: The Simplified Insolvency Programme helps distressed small and micro companies restructure, rehabilitate or wind up, while the Re-Align Framework aids contract renegotiation and compensates smaller landlords.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Simplified Insolvency Programme SIP under the Insolvency Restructuring and Dissolution (Amendment) Bill can assist financially distressed small and micro companies to restructure their debts, rehabilitate their business or to wind up the company when the business has ceased to be viable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Re-Align Framework, as provided for in the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment No 3) Bill, will assist businesses to re-negotiate and re-base their contracts, failing which, the contracts may be terminated with prospective obligations extinguished.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Re-Align Framework will also enable the smaller landlords in financial hardship to have additional compensation for early termination of contracts.

sections.label: Flow chart and legal representation query
sections.summary: A member suggests an informative flow chart for eligibility and steps, and seeks clarification on section 69's restriction on advocate and solicitor representation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One suggestion that I have is to consider introducing an informative flow chart – something similar to the handout tool issued by MinLaw to the House earlier – a navigation guide to enable businesses to better understand whether they are eligible and the steps to take to invoke the framework or SIP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I would also like to seek the following clarifications pertaining to section 69 of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment No 3) Bill, which states that "no party may be represented by an advocate and solicitor at proceedings before an adjustment relief assessor, except with the permission of the adjustment relief assessor".

sections.label: Affordable legal help for SMEs
sections.summary: A member suggests MinLaw collaborate with the Law Society on flat-rate volunteer lawyer consultation and a Community Legal Clinic for those unable to afford it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One suggestion I have after taking into consideration the concern of my Parliamentary colleague, Mr Derrick Goh, which he has shared earlier – that small and micro businesses affected are already struggling and cannot afford more costs – is for the Ministry to consider collaborating with the Law Society of Singapore to establish an enabling framework akin to what the Community Justice Centre has done for smaller claim cases, like the Primary Justice Project (PJP), where a volunteer lawyer would charge a flat rate for consultation and another flat rate if further assistance is required to file the necessary papers or prepare for the assessment hearing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The flat rate will be less than the normal market rate, taking into account what will be deemed as affordable and fair for both the client and the lawyer.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In addition, a Community Legal Clinic can also be set up specifically to assist those who are unable to afford this discounted flat rate.

sections.label: Four-month extension of time
sections.summary: A four-month universal extension of time gives contractors a legal option with more certainty besides negotiating for relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: These incremental costs are hard to capture fully but these things add up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This would provide further support for a larger portion of the value chain – support sub-contractors who would otherwise have to negotiate with main contractors under current provisions of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Indeed, there may yet be further disruption, the extent to which remains highly uncertain as rostered routine testing for construction workers continues and the possibility remains that groups of workers would continue to be quarantined from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But a four-month universal extension of time strikes a practical balance and gives contractors a legal option besides negotiating for relief, a legal option that offers more certainty.

sections.label: Support for COVID-19 Amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the amendment to the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment) Bill and urges continued improvement of testing and safety measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Under this new normal, project arrangements will be more complex, operating costs will rise and the supply of foreign workers may be interrupted from time to time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the Government's proposed amendment to the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment) Bill to provide more certainty and fairer protection for contractors, developers and the individual businesses along the entire value chain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, I would like to urge the Government to continue to improve the testing regime and safety measures such as quarantining and complement with legal measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In English): Mdm Deputy Speaker, the above notwithstanding, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It would be good to recount that in this crisis year, not only did we have five Budget Debates, through which we infused an extraordinary sum of money and implemented decisive measures in the fight against COVID-19, we also passed three Bills on Certificates of Urgency dealing with the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on businesses.

sections.label: Re-Align Framework for small businesses
sections.summary: The speaker fully supports the Re-Align Framework to help small and micro-businesses transition from the resuscitate to the rejuvenate phase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This means that small and micro businesses are particularly vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is against this context that I fully support the Re-Align Framework introduced in this COVID-19 Bill to help small and micro-businesses as we transition from the "resuscitate" phase to the "rejuvenate" phase, in the strategy that the hon Deputy Prime Minister Mr Heng Swee Keat articulated in his Ministerial speech last month.

sections.label: Re-Align Framework re-negotiation option
sections.summary: The Re-Align Framework lets small and micro-businesses with serious revenue drops re-negotiate contracts within a contained period, failing which contracts may be terminated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The Re-Align Framework offers small and micro-businesses suffering from serious drop in their revenue a ready option to re-negotiate their contracts with their counterparties within a contained period failing which the contracts may be terminated.

sections.label: Eligibility criteria based on revenue
sections.summary: Eligibility criteria in the proposed Second Schedule, Part 3 are based on SMEs' past revenue and current revenue drop, to be prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the proposed Second Schedule, Part 3 of the Bill, the eligibility criteria is to be based on the SMEs' revenue in the past and the revenue drop in the current situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: And this is proposed to be prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: Urgency for small and micro businesses
sections.summary: The speaker counters that there may not be time to debate figures because suffering small and micro-businesses would appreciate measures as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: While I can understand his approach, my respectful counter is that we may not have the benefit of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We cannot be debating on the figures because there are small and micro businesses suffering and they would appreciate these measures to be given as soon as possible.

sections.label: Publicising Re-Align Framework window
sections.summary: Small and micro-businesses have a six-week window to invoke the Re-Align Framework, so it should be publicised widely through Trade and Merchant Associations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Recognising that small and micro-businesses only have a six-week window to invoke the Re-Align Framework, it is important to publicise this framework widely especially through Trade and Merchant Associations.

sections.label: Universal EOT for construction projects
sections.summary: Part 8A of the Bill provides a universal EOT of four months covering the period when most construction projects were stopped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Part 8A of the Bill provides for a universal EOT of four months to cover the period earlier this year when most construction projects were stopped.

sections.label: EOT applies to sub-contractors
sections.summary: The proposed universal EOT will also apply to contracts between contractors and sub-contractors, as all were affected by delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: All contractors, including sub-contractors, were affected by these delays.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Hence, the proposed universal EOT will also apply to contracts between contractors and sub-contractors.

sections.label: Cost co-sharing in construction contracts
sections.summary: Part 8B requires 50% co-sharing of additional non-manpower costs in applicable construction contracts, capped at 0.2% monthly and 1.8% total of contract sum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The proposed provision in Part 8B of the Bill will require 50% co-sharing of additional non-manpower-related costs between the contracting parties in all applicable construction contracts, whether public or private.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This is subject to a monthly cap of 0.2% of the contract sum, with the total claimable amount capped at 1.8% of the contract sum.

sections.label: Revised IRDA insolvency thresholds
sections.summary: The IRDA was revised so the debt repayment scheme was extended, implemented in July 2020, moving thresholds to $150,000 for individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And then, also in relation to the insolvency thresholds, the IRDA has been revised recently so that the debt repayment scheme to ensure that individuals have a reason, have a basis on which to avoid bankruptcy had been extended, and that was implemented in July 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We moved the thresholds to $150,000 for those individuals.

sections.label: Notice triggers automatic moratorium
sections.summary: The Bill provides that service of the Notice of Negotiation itself triggers an automatic moratorium on legal and enforcement actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The answer is yes, the Bill does provide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And service of the Notice of Negotiation will itself trigger an automatic moratorium on both legal as well as enforcement actions.

sections.label: Revenue cap for small businesses
sections.summary: The revenue cap would aim to help the majority of micro and small businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I forget whether it was Mr Edward Chia or Mr Murali Pillai who asked where we would set the revenue cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We would look at, as far as possible, helping the majority of micro and small businesses.

sections.label: Using numbers instead of case evaluation
sections.summary: Numbers were chosen instead of individual forensic evaluation, and will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I have explained earlier why we chose to use a number, as opposed to having each and every case come before the Assessor to undertake an individual forensic evaluation as to whether or not this factor is part of the COVID-19 or not part of COVID-19, and whether it is mitigation and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will continue to do so and those numbers will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: Assessors' discretion on termination
sections.summary: Assessors have broad discretion to adjust the rights and obligations of the parties upon termination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Assessors, therefore, have a broad discretion to adjust the rights and obligations of the parties upon termination.

sections.label: Outstanding rental still payable
sections.summary: The Assessor cannot let a tenant under SRS walk away without outstanding rental still due to be paid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Assessor will not be able to allow a tenant to walk away from a tenancy that is under SRS without the outstanding rental still due to be paid.

sections.label: Reviewing decisions for parity
sections.summary: Minister Shanmugam and the speaker reviewed each decision to ensure parity, alignment and uniformity across Assessor panels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In many cases, particularly when we first set up the Assessor panels, both Minister Shanmugam and myself were involved in reviewing each decision, making sure that there is parity across the different Assessor panels and to really discern the different issues that come through so that there is alignment and uniformity in the decisions.

sections.label: Minister extending prescribed periods
sections.summary: The amendments clarify the Minister may extend prescribed periods by different periods, and pending applications are deemed withdrawn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, these amendments will clarify that the Minister may extend the prescribed periods under Parts 1, 2 and 3 or for description of the scheduled contracts under Part 2 of the Act by different periods of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Second, the Bill provides that applications pending at the end of the prescribed period will be deemed withdrawn.

sections.label: Rental measures prescribed dates references
sections.summary: The Bill amends Part 2 of the Act to replace references to the section 3 prescribed period with specific dates in the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Rental and Related Measures) Regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Third, to facilitate the smooth operation of Part 2 of the Act in relation to each scheduled contract, the Bill makes amendments to remove all the references to this section 3 prescribed period and instead have the provisions refer to the specific dates prescribed in the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Rental and Related Measures) Regulations.

sections.label: Separate pool of Assessors
sections.summary: A dedicated and separate pool of Assessors from the earlier COVID-19 Bills will be used for this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And so, the applications for the adjustments will also likely be more complex with regard to the schedule that we have set up and yet at the same time, need to be more timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, the mechanism that we have set up, we will require more resources and hence, we have decided that the Assessors for this Bill, will first of all be a dedicated and separate pool of Assessors from the earlier COVID-19 Bills.

sections.label: No lawyer representation before Assessors
sections.summary: Lawyers are not allowed to represent parties before the Assessors, for good reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: What we have not done is to allow for lawyers to represent the parties before the Assessors and there are good reasons for that.

sections.label: Restricting qualification criteria
sections.summary: Qualification is restricted by entity size, number of creditors, number of employees, size of debt, and realisable asset amount in liquidation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Because there is already a fairly clear criteria not only in terms of the size of the entity, but also as I outlined in my opening speech, we are also restricting qualification to number of creditors, number of employees, the size of the debt and in the context of liquidation, the amount of realisable asset.

sections.label: Exemption for experienced insolvency professionals
sections.summary: Exemption may be granted to a professional with sufficient practical insolvency experience as an approved liquidator under the predecessor Companies Act who does not meet the qualified person requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The exemption may be granted to a professional who has accrued sufficient expertise and experience, so practical experience, undertaking insolvency work as an approved liquidator under the predecessor Companies Act, but who does not presently meet the qualified person requirement.

sections.label: Employee and preferential creditor voting class
sections.summary: Under the Simplified Debt Restructuring programme, creditors with preferential debts under section 203 of IRDA vote in a separate class, each class needing two-thirds approval.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Simplified Debt Restructuring programme, in fact, through its threshold requirements, expressly recognises this position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Hence, if a company proposes to compromise debts owed to employees and other unsecured creditors with preferential debts under section 203 of IRDA, then these creditors will, as a default, vote in a separate class under the proposed section 72M(4)(b)(ii).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Each of the classes have to, on their own, pass the two-thirds threshold before the scheme will be sanctioned.

sections.label: Minister discretion for marginal companies
sections.summary: The Minister has discretion to admit companies at the margins, such as those with 51 employees, while all other criteria still apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I wish to assure Assoc Prof Jamus Lim that, first of all, this is not meant to overturn the Official Receiver's decision to admit a company into the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This allows the Minister some discretion at the margins where, if a company might, say, have 51 employees instead of 50, in all other respects, you satisfy the criteria, the Minister has the discretion to allow this company into the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This is no free pass because all the other criteria to the programme, including the continued satisfaction of the eligibility criteria, still apply to these companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is not as if it is a broad discretion, or at least that is how I heard it to be, which seems to turn the criteria upside down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It does not do that and it only allows, out of fairness, for some corporates who exist at the margins, who may not have made it into the criteria, to be considered by the Minister.
